question: What drawback does the Transformer incur from averaging attention-weighted positions, and how does multi-head attention counteract it?
reference: Relating distant positions takes a constant number of operations in the Transformer, but at the cost of reduced effective resolution due to averaging attention-weighted positions. Multi-head attention counteracts this by letting the model jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions, which averaging in a single attention head inhibits.

A self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequential operations, whereas a recurrent layer requires O(n), and convolutional layers need stacks of layers to connect all positions.
